subject: Solaris renewal: capacity tiers and blended pricing — post-call recap
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Song <emily.song@solaris.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Solaris renewal: capacity tiers and blended pricing — post-call recap

Hi Emily —

Great speaking with you and the Solaris team this morning. Quick recap and what I heard as the key asks from the call:

- Current baseline: ~6M tokens/month today (generation-heavy, ~80% chat + 20% embeddings).
- Solaris target: scale to ~15M tokens/month over the next 6–9 months, with a headroom bucket for seasonal peaks (~25M burst).
- Primary ask: a renewal that lowers unit economics vs. today and covers an expected route addition for embeddings + a second model for higher-quality summaries.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a budget band of $800–$1,000 per 1M tokens as the target for blended pricing across routes.

Attached I dropped two artifacts: a short blend worked example (redwood-blend-examples.pdf) and the volume model you shared back on the call (solaris-volume-models.csv).

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) Redwood to propose 2 blended scenarios (conservative and aggressive) and one step-up cadence (3-month and 6-month thresholds).
2) Provide a quick sensitivity table showing blended $/1M as embeddings are added (embeddings are ~0.25x gen cost per token but high volume).
3) Share a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and procurement contacts — I’m attaching a draft.

I’ll loop in Marissa to draft the commercial scenarios; Vivek will add a short note on routing/tech levers that change unit economics (caching, quantization, model mix).

Availability: I can do a 30-min pricing walk-through Tue or Thu morning PST. What works for you?

Thanks —
Hannah

Subject: Re: Solaris renewal: capacity tiers and blended pricing — post-call recap

Thanks Hannah — this captures it well. A few clarifications from my side:

- The 15M target is our mid-plan; leadership will sign for the conservative 10M if economics push higher. Ideally we want to see a path to <$1,000 / 1M tokens blended at 15M.
- Embeddings will likely be a separate ingest pipeline but we want the commercial to reflect blended unit economics (so both routes in one contract).
- Can you show a stepped discount that triggers at 10M and 20M (both cumulative monthly averages) rather than a single threshold? That’s our preferred buying pattern.

I’ve added procurement so they can confirm any internal contract cadence. Tue 10am PST works for a quick walk-through — I’ll take the invite.

Thanks,
Emily

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-04T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Solaris renewal — tech note on routes and unit econ

Looping in a short engineering perspective that we can include in the pricing appendix: 

Key points that materially affect blended $/1M:
- Route mix: embeddings are much lower cost per token in our serving profiles (roughly 0.2–0.3x gen cost depending on model). If Solaris routes 40% of tokens to embeddings, blended rate falls significantly.
- Model mix: adding a higher-quality summarization model (larger weights) increases cost per token on that route — but can be mitigated by aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated user sessions.
- Optimizations: quantized model variants + continuous batching can shave ~15–25% off baseline gen costs for steady-state load.

Worked example (rough):
- Scenario A (conservative): 10M tokens/month, 85% gen @ $1,200/1M, 15% embeddings @ $300/1M => blended ~ $1,065/1M.
- Scenario B (aggressive): 15M tokens/month, 70% gen @ $1,100/1M, 30% embeddings @ $300/1M => blended ~ $880/1M.

I can prepare a short spreadsheet with per-route assumptions and the weighted blended output — will attach to the MAP before the Tue call.

-Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
